statement: In the planted observation law Xv(t) = tσv +Bv(t), every finite subvector of (Wv)v∈V is a standard vector Brownian motion in both the raw observation filtration (F0 t ) and its usual augmentation (Ft). In particular W has product Wiener law. The posterior means have continuous versions, starting at zero, and mv(t) = X u∈V Z t 0 Cvu(s) dWu(s). (4.2) At each fixed time these versions are E[σv | Ft], and Cvu is the covariance conditional on Ft. The site fields and the component fields can be chosen as jointly Borel, progressively measurable functions of time and observation history that are continuous in time almost surely. For every input, the chosen function hv→w(t) uses only observations in Tv→w through time t. Almost surely the cavity identities and the bounds (2.5) then hold simultaneously at all times and all their indices. With the response coefficients cvu from (2.6) and Av = P u c2 vu from (3.11), the continuous site field satisfies the equation below. In every integral, Av is assigned value zero wherever this sum is infinite. hv(t) = X u∈V Z t 0 cvu(s) dWu(s) + Z t 0 mv(s)Av(s) ds. (4.3) Each Brownian sum in this proposition converges, along any exhaustion by finite vertex sets, in the norm ∥Z∥M2 T = E sup 0≤t≤T |Z(t)|2 !1/2 (T < ∞). The drift in (4.3) is absolutely integrable on each such horizon almost surely and in expectation.
